body: Thank you for the repro! We'll definitely incorporate this into our test suite. Hi @JoanFM , sorry for the delay and thanks for the test! Looks like this happens for non-async client and server too, I created a Bazel test [here](https://github.com/XuanWang-Amos/grpc/blob/fixit_JinaHanging/src/python/grpcio_tests/tests/unit/_jina_hanging_test.py) to help debug.

This is the command for the test: `bazel test --test_timeout=10 "//src/python/grpcio_tests/tests/unit:_jina_hanging_test.native"`, and one of two things can happen:
* Test will fail without any error message (a segfault in core).
* Test will timeout after 10s.

I did some digging and here is what I know so far:

* It was caused by a segfault in core when calling [gpr_atm_no_barrier_load](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/src/core/lib/iomgr/lockfree_event.cc#L216).
* `state_` is invalid here:
```
(gdb) p this->state_
Cannot access memory at address 0x7fff74000e00
```
* By checking backwards, `state_` is coming from [data_ptr](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/src/core/lib/iomgr/ev_epoll1_linux.cc#L675), and used in [fd_become_writable](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/src/core/lib/iomgr/ev_epoll1_linux.cc#L699), looks like `ev` is valid but not the `data_ptr`:
```
(gdb) p ev
$8 = (epoll_event *) 0x7ffff7301c84 <g_epoll_set+4>
(gdb) p *ev
$9 = {events = 4, data = {ptr = 0x7fff74000df1, fd = 1946160625, u32 = 1946160625, u64 = 140735139548657}}
(gdb) p *(ev->data.ptr)
Attempt to dereference a generic pointer.
(gdb) p *(int*)(ev->data.ptr)
Cannot access memory at address 0x7fff74000df1
```
* Using bisect, I'm able to locate the Culprit PR: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/30101/, it was released in `v1.48.0-pre1` so `1.47.2` was working as expected.


Since I'm not an expert for Core, @ctiller can you help take a look?

Thanks @XuanWang-Amos for your detailed explanation and for the effort on chasing such a tough one.

Hopefully people with knowledgr from the core can help us out here.

Hello @ctiller ,

Let me know if you need any help from me or if I can help in any manner to clarify or debug the issue.

I have tried to look at the code, and with the little knowledge I have, I think that the only explanation possible is that:

`do_poll_wait` is not called before to fill the `buffer` pointed by the `events`.

I am not sure who is freeing the memory (who owns that memory) and may be releasing at shutdown.

> I have tried to look at the code, and with the little knowledge I have, I think that the only explanation possible is that:
> 
> `do_poll_wait` is not called before to fill the `buffer` pointed by the `events`.
> 
> I am not sure who is freeing the memory (who owns that memory) and may be releasing at shutdown.

Another possibility and that seems quite strange to me, is that when calling `epoll_set_shutdown` the `cursor` and `num_events` is not also reset to `0`.
